paper.title: A model for spatial conflict (the voter model)

headline: Voter fixation (agent-based): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; P(all-up) tracks u [u=0.2:P=0.200, u=0.5:P=0.460, u=0.8:P=0.790]; consensus rate 1.000

verdicts.gate: P1 every run reaches absorbing consensus (consensus rate = 1.0 at every u)
P2 P(all-up) within +/-0.07 of u for every u in [0.2, 0.5, 0.8]
P3 mean final magnetization within +/-0.1 of 2u-1 for every u

extra.metric: P(fixation to all-up) = fraction of runs ending all-1
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model (mean-field / complete-graph voter); no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the fixation=initial-density result and would catch an artifact

citations: Clifford, P. & Sudbury, A. (1973). A model for spatial conflict. Biometrika 60(3):581-588. doi:10.1093/biomet/60.3.581.

Holley, R.A. & Liggett, T.M. (1975). Ergodic theorems for weakly interacting infinite systems and the voter model. Ann. Probab. 3(4):643-663. doi:10.1214/aop/1176996306. (consensus / clustering; mean-field fixation prob = initial density, magnetization conserved in expectation).

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction validated against the mean-field anchors P(all-up)=u and mean magnetization=2u-1
